la:verb:tulo.html:
tulo, tĕtŭli (tŭli), 3, v. a.
akin with tollo; Gr. τλάω
, ante-class. collat. form of fero,
to bring, bear, lift up: nisi quid tua facultas nobis tulat opem, peream, Att. ap. Macr. Diff. et Soc. Gr. et Lat. Verb. 6, 14 (Trag. Frag. v. 102 Rib.); cf. ; and v. fero init.

senses: A daughter of M. Tullius Cicero
la:adj:Tullius.html:
Tullĭus, i, m.; Tullĭa, ae, f.,
the name of a Roman gens. Esp.,
Servius Tullius, the sixth king of Rome, sqq. —
M. Tullius Cicero, the renowned statesman and orator.—
Q. Tullius Cicero, his brother.—
M. Tullius Tiro, a freedman of M. Cicero.—
Fem. Tullia, a daughter of king Servius Tullius, and wife of Tarquinius Superbus.—Also,
A daughter of M. Tullius Cicero.—Hence, Tullĭā-nus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to a Tullius, Tullian: semis,: caput,: Scipio, i. e. introduced in Cicero's Somnium Scipionis, .—Subst.: Tullĭānum, i, n., the dungeon of the state-prison in Rome, built by king Servius Tullius, Müll.; ; ; cf. Becker, Antiq. 1, p. 262 sq.—Adv.: Tullĭānē, in the manner of M. Tullius Cicero: jocari, Aug. contr. Pelag. 2, 10, 37.
